title: a results page saved for a fetch step's own search
line: a results page is told from a record page by the parser that claims it, never the file name, and goes to the fetch step whose citation was searched for by that name in that collection, as the run's own artifact with the query as run: none when no row fits, the rows kept on the artifact, the step planned, the page filed under the tree; the same search saved again in the browser, other bytes and the same rows, is a repeat, already answered on these fields, and is removed with nothing new to log

steps.say: the search saved, under a name of the owner's own

expect.why: read as a results page by its own markup; it fulfils the fetch step whose citation was searched for by this name in this collection; the page names her only as a mother with no dates, so no row fits and the run is none
the step's log row: none, the reason and the count in its note, the query as run, the page as its artifact
archived under the holder with the search URL as locator
a none run leaves the step planned
the twenty rows stay on the artifact as candidates
the page leaves the inbox, filed under the tree

steps.say: Reiko Diane Davidson's search of FamilySearch's New Jersey marriages saved, as the archive holds it: it fulfils her 1988 marriage step and her husband's, whose citation was searched for by her name in that collection; none of its five rows fits

expect.why: the citation's own search at the holder, for both people the marriage citation names
one run on her step, the page its artifact

steps.say: the same search saved again in the browser two and a half hours later, as the archive holds it: other bytes, the same five rows, the steps already answered on these very fields

expect.why: a repeat is answered, not archived again
nothing new to archive: the file is removed as a repeat
the repeat logs no second run
